title: How to find your way out of a food desert

parts.label: Part 1
parts.title: How to find your way out of a food desert
parts.subtitle: Ordinary citizens have been using the internet to draw attention to the lack of healthy eating options in inner cities.
parts.article:
Food desert

(A) Over the last few months, a survey has been carried out of over 200 greengrocers and convenience stores in Crown Heights, a neighborhood in Brooklyn, New York. As researchers from the Brooklyn Food Association enter the details, colorful dots appear on their online map, which display the specific location of each of the food stores in a handful of central Brooklyn neighborhoods. Clicking on a dot will show you the store’s name and whether it carries fresh fruit and vegetables, wholegrain bread, low-fat dairy and other healthy options.

(B) The researchers plan eventually to survey the entire borough of Brooklyn. ‘We want to get to a more specific and detailed description of what that looks like,’ says Jeffrey Heehs, who leads the project. He hopes it will help residents find fresh food in urban areas where the stores sell mostly packaged snacks or fast food, areas otherwise known as food deserts. The aim of the project is also to assist government officials in assessing food availability, and in forming future policies about what kind of food should be sold and where.

(C) In fact, the Brooklyn project represents the intersection of two growing trends: mapping fresh food markets in US cities, and private citizens creating online maps of local neighborhood features. According to Michael Goodchild, a geographer at the University of California at Santa Barbara, citizen map makers may make maps because there is no good government map, or to record problems such as burned-out traffic lights.

(D) According to recent studies, people at higher risk of chronic disease and who receive minimal incomes for the work they do frequently live in neighborhoods located in food deserts. But how did these food deserts arise? Linda Alwitt and Thomas Donley, marketing researchers at DePaul University in Chicago, found that supermarkets often can’t afford the amount of land required for their stores in cities. City planning researcher Cliff Guy and colleagues at the University of Leeds in the UK found in 2004 that smaller urban groceries tend to close due to competition from suburban supermarkets.

(E) As fresh food stores leave a neighborhood, residents find it harder to eat well and stay healthy. Food deserts are linked with lower local health outcomes, and they may be a driving force in the health disparities between lower-income and affluent people in the US. Until recently, the issue attracted little national attention, and received no ongoing funding for research.

(F) Now, more US cities are becoming aware of their food landscapes. Last year, the United States Department of Agriculture launched a map of where food stores are located in all the US counties. Mari Gallagher, who runs a private consulting firm, says her researchers have mapped food stores and related them to health statistics for the cities of Detroit, Chicago, Cincinnati and Washington, DC. These maps help cities identify where food deserts are and, occasionally, have documented that people living in food deserts have higher rates of diet-related diseases.

(G) The Brooklyn project differs in that it’s run by a local core of five volunteers who have worked on the project for the past year, rather than trained, academic researchers. To gather data, they simply go to individual stores with pre-printed surveys in hand, and once the storekeeper’s permission has been obtained, check off boxes on their list against the products for sale in the store. Their approach to data collection and research has been made possible by technologies such as mapping software and GPS-related smart phones, Google Maps and OpenStreetMap, an open-source online map with a history of involvement in social issues. Like Brooklyn Food Association volunteers, many citizen online map makers use maps to bring local problems to official attention, Goodchild says.

(H) Heehs, the mapping project leader, says that after his group gathers more data, it will compare neighborhoods, come up with solutions to address local needs, and then present them to New York City officials. Their website hasn’t caught them much local or official attention yet, however. It was launched only recently, but its creators haven’t yet set up systems to see who’s looking at it.

(I) Experts who visited the Brooklyn group’s site were optimistic but cautious. ‘This kind of detailed information could be very useful,’ says Michele Ver Ploeg, an economist for the Department of Agriculture. To make the map more helpful to both residents and policy makers, she would like to see price data for healthy products, too. Karen Ansel, a registered dietician and a spokesperson for the American Dietetic Association, found the site confusing to navigate. ‘That said, with this information in place the group has the tools to build a more user-friendly site that could be … very helpful to consumers,’ she says. ‘The group also should ensure their map is available to those who don’t have internet access at home,’ she adds. In fact, a significant proportion of Brooklyn residents don’t have internet access at home and 8 percent rely on dial-up service, instead of high-speed internet access, according to Gretchen Maneval, director of Brooklyn College’s Center for the Study of Brooklyn. ‘It’s still very much a work in progress,’ Heehs says of the online map. They’ll start advertising it online and by email to other community groups, such as urban food garden associations, next month. He also hopes warmer days in the spring will draw out fresh volunteers to spread awareness and to finish surveying, as they have about two-thirds of Brooklyn left to cover.

analyses.content: 你可能被后面的“fresh fruit”之类干扰，但题目已经用“details of its produce”把这些具体食物概括了，填剩余的并列项“location”即可。

As researchers from the Brooklyn Food Association enter the details, colorful dots appear on their online map, which display the specific location of each of the food stores in a handful of central Brooklyn neighborhoods. Clicking on a dot will show you the store’s name and whether it carries fresh fruit and vegetables, wholegrain bread, low-fat dairy and other healthy options.
题目问地图提供了商店名字、产品细节和什么，原文明确提到地图上的点展示了每个商店的“具体位置”（location），点击后还能看到名字和产品。
题目问项目的目标之一是帮助制定关于食物的新的什么，原文明确说到目的是协助政府官员形成未来的“政策”（policies）。
你可能想填“government”或者“officials”，但题目问的是“develop new...”对应原文的“forming future...”，填制定的产物即可。
The aim of the project is also to assist government officials in assessing food availability, and in forming future policies about what kind of food should be sold and where.
题目问当什么地图不令人满意时市民会去制作地图，原文直接说市民做地图是因为没有好的“政府”（government）地图。
你可能想填“good”，但这里需要填一个名词来修饰maps，说明是谁出的地图不好。

In fact, the Brooklyn project represents the intersection of two growing trends: mapping fresh food markets in US cities, and private citizens creating online maps of local neighborhood features. According to Michael Goodchild, a geographer at the University of California at Santa Barbara, citizen map makers may make maps because there is no good government map, or to record problems such as burned-out traffic lights.
你可能想填“disease”，但原文说的是患病风险高（higher risk），而题目问的是什么比较低（low），所以只能是收入。
题目问住在食物沙漠的人通常有什么比较低，原文说这些地区的人获得的“收入”（incomes）最少，minimal对应题目的low。
According to recent studies, people at higher risk of chronic disease and who receive minimal incomes for the work they do frequently live in neighborhoods located in food deserts.
题目问超市在城里买不起足够的什么来建店，原文提到超市经常负担不起在城市建店所需的“土地”（land）数量。
你可能顺着“买不起”想找钱相关的词，但原文“can't afford”后面直接跟的就是买不起的实体对象“土地”。
Linda Alwitt and Thomas Donley, marketing researchers at DePaul University in Chicago, found that supermarkets often can’t afford the amount of land required for their stores in cities.
题目问城市里的小型杂货店通常无法应对超市的什么，原文说它们倒闭是因为来自郊区超市的“竞争”（competition）。
你可能顺着“cope with（应对）”去找动词，但这里需要填一个名词，说明打败这些小店的原因。
City planning researcher Cliff Guy and colleagues at the University of Leeds in the UK found in 2004 that smaller urban groceries tend to close due to competition from suburban supermarkets.

groups.description:
Complete the notes below.
Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
Write your answers in boxes 1–6 on your answer sheet.

questions.question: A group of professional researchers are in charge of the Brooklyn project.

analyses.content: The Brooklyn project differs in that it’s run by a local core of five volunteers who have worked on the project for the past year, rather than trained, academic researchers.
你可能看到前面段落提到了researchers就直接选TRUE，但一定要注意这段明确说了Brooklyn项目的特殊之处就在于它“不是”专业人员做的。
题目说这个项目由专业研究人员负责，但原文明确指出它是由志愿者运行的，“而不是”（rather than）受过训练的学术研究人员。

questions.question: The Brooklyn project team carries out their assessment of stores without the owner’s knowledge.

analyses.content: 题目说团队在店主不知情的情况下进行评估，但原文说他们“一旦获得了店主的许可”（permission has been obtained）才开始打钩记录，说明店主完全知情。
你可能没注意到题目里的“without”这个否定词，或者没看懂“permission”是许可的意思，导致意思理解反了。

To gather data, they simply go to individual stores with pre-printed surveys in hand, and once the storekeeper’s permission has been obtained, check off boxes on their list against the products for sale in the store.

questions.question: The Brooklyn project has experienced technical difficulties setting up the website.

analyses.content: 题目说项目在建立网站时遇到了技术困难，原文只说网站最近刚上线，还没建立查看访客的系统，并没有提到遭遇了任何“技术困难”。
你可能看到“还没建立系统”就自己脑补成了他们技术不行遇到困难了，但原文没交代原因，做题切忌自己瞎猜。
Their website hasn’t caught them much local or official attention yet, however. It was launched only recently, but its creators haven’t yet set up systems to see who’s looking at it.

questions.question: The city government has taken a considerable interest in the Brooklyn project website.

analyses.content: Heehs, the mapping project leader, says that after his group gathers more data, it will compare neighborhoods, come up with solutions to address local needs, and then present them to New York City officials. Their website hasn’t caught them much local or official attention yet, however.
题目说市政府对这个网站产生了极大的兴趣，原文却打脸说网站“还没有引起太多当地或官方的关注”。
你可能把上一句“准备提交给纽约官员”当成了官员已经关注了，要分清“计划去做”和“已经发生”的区别。

questions.question: Michele Ver Ploeg believes the Brooklyn project website should contain additional information.

analyses.content: 题目说这个人认为网站应该包含额外信息，原文明确提到她希望能“也看到健康产品的价格数据”（see price data too），确实是要求增加信息。
你可能只看了第28句她在夸网站有用，没往下看第29句她紧接着提出的改进建议。

‘This kind of detailed information could be very useful,’ says Michele Ver Ploeg, an economist for the Department of Agriculture. To make the map more helpful to both residents and policy makers, she would like to see price data for healthy products, too.

questions.question: The rate of internet use in Brooklyn is unlikely to increase in the near future.

analyses.content: 题目说布鲁克林的网络使用率在不久的将来不太可能增加，原文只交代了目前的网络覆盖率情况，完全没预测未来的趋势。
你可能根据原文说的“很多人没网”就自己推理出未来也没戏，但原文没写未来的事情就是没给，不能靠常识答题。

In fact, a significant proportion of Brooklyn residents don’t have internet access at home and 8 percent rely on dial-up service, instead of high-speed internet access, according to Gretchen Maneval, director of Brooklyn College’s Center for the Study of Brooklyn.

questions.question: Jeffrey Heehs would like more people to assist with the Brooklyn project research.

analyses.content: 题目说负责人希望更多人来协助项目研究，原文提到他希望春天能吸引“新的志愿者”（fresh volunteers）来完成调查。
你可能不认识“draw out fresh volunteers”（吸引新的志愿者），或者没反应过来这就是题目里“more people to assist”的同义替换。
He also hopes warmer days in the spring will draw out fresh volunteers to spread awareness and to finish surveying, as they have about two-thirds of Brooklyn left to cover.
